ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L.561-1 to L.561-59 and R.561-1 to R.561-59 (AML/CFT obligations); Decree No. 2017-1094 of 12 June 2017 (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs - RBE); Code de commerce, Articles L.123-1 ff., L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL registration and UBO declaration at the RCS); EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 (AML4) as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AML5); AMF and ACPR guidelines; TRACFIN reporting framework for cash-intensive restaurant operations.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of UBOs, directors, and beneficial shareholders against: (i) TRACFIN and French asset-freezing lists (Fichier des avoirs gelés); (ii) EU consolidated financial sanctions lists and Council Regulations (EU) 269/2014 and 833/2014; (iii) UN Security Council consolidated lists; (iv) OFAC SDN list where USD clearing or correspondent banking is involved (applied as a de facto standard by French banks). PEP determination follows Article L.561-10 CMF and R.561-18 to R.561-20-3 CMF, covering domestic and foreign PEPs, family members, and close associates; enhanced due diligence is mandatory for PEP relationships and high-risk third-country origins; compliance with ACPR Guidelines 2020-08 and 2023-07 is required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), operated with Infogreffe and the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI); national name availability screening via data.inpi.fr and the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RNCS) database.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names (dénomination sociale) must use Latin alphabetic characters; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into French-compatible spelling. French language is mandatory under Article L.221-3 of the Consumer Code for commercial documentation and signage; a foreign-language name is permissible if it is not contrary to French public policy and does not reproduce a prior trademark or prohibited token. The corporate name must be distinguishable from existing RNCS registrations and from protected trademarks in France and the EU.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a statutory 30-day name reservation certificate. A name is provisionally protected from the date of electronic submission via the Guichet Unique until registration is completed (typically 4-10 business days), and definitively protected upon RCS registration. Upon rejection by the Greffier (registrar) for identity, confusing similarity, or public policy grounds, the applicant may: (i) resubmit an amended name through the Guichet Unique at no additional statutory fee; (ii) file a formal challenge against the registrar's decision before the President of the competent Tribunal judiciaire (commercial chamber) within 15 days of notification, by requête; and (iii) for trademark-based conflicts, initiate opposition before the INPI within 2 months of publication of the conflicting French trademark application. Legal counsel should concurrently purchase priority through INPI trademark filing in class 43 to secure the hotpot brand.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only through an approved domiciliation provider (société de domiciliation) for a statutory maximum of five years from incorporation (Article L.123-11-2 Code de commerce). A virtual office cannot serve as the registered operating premises for the restaurant licence, hygiene registration (DDETSPP), or to hold the débit de boissons licence; the physical hotpot dining premises must be separately declared and compliant with fire-safety and sanitary regulations. The registered office may be distinct from the operating site provided that a visible signpost discloses the registered office address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified first-24-month risk profile: 100% mandatory pre-opening inspection by the municipal fire-safety commission (commission de sécurité) for dining capacity above 20 persons; 30-45% likelihood of unannounced food-hygiene inspection by DDETSPP within the first 12 months; 10-15% likelihood of URSSAF/Inspection du travail social compliance inspections; less than 5% likelihood of an unannounced physical visit by the commercial registry or tax authorities to the registered office itself.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL formation and governance); Decree No. 2023-310 on the Single Business Formalities Portal; General Tax Code Article 809-II (registration duty).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) for the planned registered office; filings submitted electronically through the Guichet Unique operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Société à Responsabilité Limitée incorporation file comprising the statuts (Articles of Association), Declaration M0 (demande d'immatriculation), Blocked Capital Attestation, and Legal Notice publication certificate
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for a SARL (share capital freely fixed in the statuts; must be fully paid-up in cash at incorporation). All cash contributions must be deposited to a blocked escrow account with a bank or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, and may not be released to the Gérant until the certificate of incorporation is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the duly convened general meeting of shareholders of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée to be incorporated under French law: (1) the Articles of Association are hereby adopted and the stated share capital is fully subscribed and allotted; (2) all cash contributions are deemed paid in and deposited in escrow; (3) the registered office is fixed at the address set out in the Articles; (4) Mr./Ms. [Name], present and accepting, is appointed Gérant with powers to act in all ordinary transactions, open bank accounts, and bind the company; (5) the Gérant is expressly authorized to effect the capital release, publish the legal notice, and apply for incorporation with the Commercial Court Registry; (6) formation expenses are accepted and charged to the company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability and National Company Identifier Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) via the official formalities portal (guichet-unique.inpi.fr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online pre-filing inquiry to verify that the proposed corporate name, including any device or trademark, does not infringe existing registered trademarks or company names and is distinct within the national trade register (Registre National des Entreprises). Confirm the availability of the intended registered office address for service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name is refused or conflicting, file a change request with an amended corporate name and pay a resubmission fee; in case of unfair refusal of a filing, lodge an appeal with the INPI Director General within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Articles and Payment of Corporate Registration Duty
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any French notary or the shareholders' legal counsel; the enacted Articles must be appended to the filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize and sign the statuts by all shareholders. If the contributions are cash-only, the Articles may be executed under private seal (sous seing privé) and then registered with the relevant tax office to pay fixed registration duty (droit fixe) of €375 applied to the share capital; alternatively, a notarial act is mandatory only where non-cash assets (real property) are contributed.
required_dossiers: Statement of subscription and payment of shares
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office issues a query, correct the capital statement and re-file the act; the registration duty is a fixed fee independent of capital, no appraisal disputes expected for cash capital contributions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocked Capital Deposit and Attestation of Cash Contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A French commercial bank, including online business banks, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary escrow account in the name of the company in formation and deposit 100% of the subscribed cash capital. At the end of the blocking period, the depositary bank issues a certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds) identifying the subscribers, the amount, and the exact share allocations, which is mandatory for inclusion in the registration file.
required_dossiers: Notarized or private-signature Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays the attestation, request a formal written justification and, after five business days, engage an alternate credit institution for a new deposit; the deposit remains irrevocable until the registry issues the Kbis extract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Statutory Legal Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A legally recognized journal d'annonces légales (JAL) approved for the department of the registered office; filing made online via an approved legal notice platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within eight days from the signature of the Articles, publish a formation notice containing the corporate name, form, capital, registered office, duration, object, and identity of the Gérant. Obtain the certificate of publication and retain the issue receipt; the notice is a prerequisite to the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Kbis or name certificate of any predecessor entity (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL rejects the notice for incomplete content, correct and republish the announcement within 48 hours; time lost does not prejudice the registration unless the eight-day deadline passes after completion of correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Dossier to the Commercial Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (application through the INPI Guichet Unique online Single Formalities Portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form M0 through the Guichet Unique, attach the executed Articles, capital deposit attestation, publication certificate, proof of registered office, and identity documents, and submit the electronic file with payment of the greffe fee (approximately €50 for the RCS registration plus portal fee). The registry verifies compliance and issues the certificate of incorporation and Kbis extract; INSEE then delivers SIREN/SIRET numbers.
required_dossiers: Certificate of publication in a legal notice journal
Proof of address of registered office (lease or utility bill)
Identity and non-conviction declaration of the Gérant
Payment receipt of the registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a non-compliance query (procès-verbal de carence or request for particulars), cure the omission within one month by submitting the corrected annex; if registration is refused, file a procedural appeal before the Judge supervising the Directory of the Registries or the President of the commercial court, and, for portal submission issues, contest the INPI decision within two months before the administrative court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Préfecture du département, Inspection du Travail (DREETS) and Direction Départementale de la Protection des Populations (DDPP) / Direction Générale de la Concurrence, de la Consommation et de la Répression des Fraudes (DGCCRF)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registration of a foodservice establishment (Déclaration d'ouverture d'un établissement de restauration) and, where alcoholic beverages are placed on the table, a Licence de débit de boissons (catégorie II or III) with the competences of the Mairie and an approved Permis d'Exploitation training module

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) and the Local Sanitation Authority (Service Public d'Assainissement Non Collectif / gestionnaire du réseau)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration only; hotpot restaurants under a floor area of 200 m² are outside the ICPE (Installations Classées) authorization regime, but the activity is deemed ICPE designation 2215 (Restaurant and beverage service) under the régime de déclaration when serving alcohol or exceeding the low-capacity threshold; a simplified registration dossier with an hourly rate compliance sheet is required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Mandatory grease trap and oil-water separator ahead of any sewer connection; fats, oils and greases (FOGs) limited to 100 mg/L, suspended solids 60 mg/L, COD 125 mg/L at point of discharge under the municipal sewerage conventions; waste cooking oil UCO must be collected by a registered waste carrier with e-tracking paperwork; kitchen ventilation must comply with the French Code de l'Environnement odor threshold (no nuisance beyond property boundary) and the ERP fire exhaust standards; solid waste segregation and HACCP temperature logs are required as part of the hygiene approval

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Commission inspection of the premises as a 5th-category ERP (Type N restaurant) with a favorable fire safety decision (avis favorable) before opening; structural load inspection certificate for the dining mezzanine and extraction equipment; Declaration of Conformity to Accessiblity law; workplace clearance from DREETS (occupational safety) including the single-risk assessment document, mandatory chef/kitchen worker safety briefings, and the employer's registration at the health insurance and joint occupational risk appendix.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) of France; official portal: impots.gouv.fr; company/VAT registration entry: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign investor forms the SARL through the Guichet Unique (INPI) portal; after incorporation INSEE assigns SIREN/SIRET, and DGFiP issues the TVA intra-community number. Non-established suppliers registering directly for VAT must submit Form CA1 to the local SIE and, if outside the EU, appoint a fiscal representative and obtain an individual VAT number under article 286 CGI.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no general check-the-box regime. An eligible SARL de famille may elect, under article 239 bis AA CGI, to be taxed as a pass-through partnership; otherwise the SARL is subject to corporate income tax. Anti-hybrid mismatch elections are not available; statutory anti-hybrid classification rules apply ex officio.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Established taxable persons must obtain a VAT number irrespective of turnover. Franchise exemption thresholds are EUR 36,800 for services and EUR 91,900 for goods, but do not exempt registration; non-EU sellers have a zero threshold and any physical supply or restaurant activity in France creates immediate VAT nexus.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B e-invoicing and B2C e-reporting phased in from 2026/2027 through a certified platform (PDP) and the State public portal (PPF); all B2C cash receipts in restaurants require anti-fraud certified cash-register software that captures and archives transaction data with digital signature sequence; no separate real-time stamping yet, but fiscal data must be available on DGFiP request.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to a non-EU destination are zero-rated under article 262 CGI when the seller proves material dispatch/transport out of the EU. Intra-EU supplies to VAT-numbered business customers are zero-rated under article 262 ter I CGI. Cross-border B2B services (including supports for overseas branches) are French VAT-excluded by place-of-supply rules, if the customer is established outside France.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 confirming repatriated export payment
Proof of dispatch or export license/permit applied to the goods
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating is rigorously audited by DGFiP; unsupported credits are delinked with 0.2% monthly interest and 5% late-filing surcharge. In bad faith, a 80% penalty under CGI art. 1729 applies; organized evasion triggers 100% penalty and publication of the sanction. Criminal tax fraud under art. 1741 CGI is punishable by up to five years imprisonment and €75,000 fine.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (central bank and monetary authority); Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR), the French banking and conduct-supervision authority attached to Banque de France; Direction Générale du Trésor, Ministry of Economy and Finance, for foreign-exchange policy, capital-movement oversight and balance-of-payments reporting. Banque de France operates interbank clearing oversight and payment-system supervision in France.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions in France. Cross-border capital movements between EU Member States are liberalised under the free movement of capital provisions of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, and France applies no systemic exchange-control approvals for ordinary corporate financing, equity contributions, supplier settlements, or profit remittances. The main practical hurdles are not convertibility but compliance verification: proof of lawful source of funds, beneficial-ownership disclosure, and confirmation that the counterparty is not subject to EU or French sanctions. Dividends distributed by the French SARL may be remitted freely to the foreign shareholder without prior Bank de France approval; however, a final withholding tax may apply under Article 119 bis-2 of the French General Tax Code unless reduced by an applicable double-tax treaty or exempted under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if the shareholder owns at least 10% of the SARL and satisfies all holding-period and anti-abuse conditions. A French company receiving foreign exchange income is not obliged to obtain a licence, but all accounting entries must ultimately be measured and reported in euros under French GAAP.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no mandatory surrender or forced conversion of export proceeds into euros. Export receipts in foreign currency may be credited to a foreign-currency account or converted at market rates at the SARL's discretion. There is no statutory timeline within which export proceeds must be repatriated or converted. Nevertheless, all foreign-currency-denominated receivables and cash balances must be valued in euros for French financial statements and tax reporting. Any physical import or export of euro-denominated or foreign-currency banknotes, securities, cheques, or other bearer negotiable instruments having a total value of EUR 10,000 or more must be declared to French Customs pursuant to Article L152-1 of the French Monetary and Financial Code and Regulation (EC) No 1889/2005. Failure to declare may lead to customs seizure and penalties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Blocked Account and Commercial Current Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High as a supplementary operating account, but Low as the sole banking relationship and Low for statutory SARL capital escrow. Licensed French and EU electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as ACPR-authorised fintechs or EU-passported alternative payment institutions are viable for day-to-day supplier disbursements, payroll execution, and cross-border treasury concentration because they offer fast onboarding, virtual IBANs, and lower fees. Legal constraints under the French Monetary and Financial Code and the EU Electronic Money Directive are material: an EMI is not a credit institution, cannot accept deposits that require a banking licence, cannot grant credit, cannot issue the statutory certificate of deposit required for SARL incorporation, and must safeguard client funds in separate accounts held at an authorised credit institution. For French tax levies, social-security contributions, payroll direct debits, and merchant acquiring for a walk-in hotpot restaurant, a full bank current account remains necessary. EMIs are therefore recommended for inbound-outbound payment routing only and never as a proxy for a French banking-relationship mandate.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under applicable French anti-money-laundering law (Articles L561-1 et seq. of the Monetary and Financial Code) and ACPR guidelines, a bank may perform KYC by reliable independent electronic data, video-identification, and qualified electronic signatures, so a physical branch visit is not uniformly mandatory in every case. In practice, for a newly incorporated SARL with non-resident shareholders or with directors not domiciled in France, the bank will require either an in-branch interview or a high-grade interactive video call before opening the dossier. If the SARL's management is entirely overseas, opening may be refused unless a duly authorised French-resident representative or a notarially appointed company manager appears physically. The merchant-acquiring and POS component for the hotpot restaurant adds a mandatory site-compliance and operational inspection because the business is consumer-facing and will process physical card-present transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial equity injection from a non-EEA shareholder without a credible source-of-wealth trail, particularly when multiple rapid transfers arrive before the SARL has a French operating history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sworn shareholder declarations of source of funds and wealth, personal or parent-company bank statements covering at least the last six months, audited financial statements or income-tax returns of the provider of capital, notarised and apostilled identity documents, an accurate ownership diagram showing each ultimate beneficial owner, and a written narrative explaining the overseas hotpot restaurant expansion plan and anticipated capital expenditure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business-profile mismatch: the SARL is registered under ISIC 5610 as a full-service dining and condiment-supply chain, but projected revenue appears dominated by anonymous cash flows or POS transactions with insufficient documented supplier or inventory chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly signed lease agreement for the French restaurant premises, projected budgets and cash-flow forecasts, supplier contracts with hotpot base producers and condiment wholesalers, invoices for kitchen equipment and fit-out works, hygiene and food-safety approvals from the direction départementale de la protection des populations, projected daily-cash reconciliation policy, payroll plan, and a signed merchant-acquiring agreement with a licensed acquirer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border trade disbursements to jurisdictions with sanctions exposure, tax-secrecy ratings, or high-risk payment corridors for imported hotpot ingredients, especially when wire-payment instructions do not clearly match commercial invoices.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formalised import contracts, commercial invoices, packing lists, transport bills of lading, customs declarations, Incoterms evidence, import approvals or food-import certificates, supplier KYC and sanctions-screening results, proof of transport payments, and bank-compliant payment narratives linking every MT103 instruction to a specific shipment and order number.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity or statutory inconsistency: the SARL does not declare its beneficial owners to the French company register, uses a non-resident nominal manager, or presents stamp-charged statutes that are not translated or legalised for banking purposes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed registre des bénéficiaires effectifs filed with the commercial court greffe, sworn French translation of the SARL statutes, apostilled certificates of incorporation and good standing for all overseas corporate shareholders, notarised powers of attorney for each manager, valid passport and proof of residence for every person with a 25% or greater economic interest, and a corporate resolution authorising bank account opening and signatory roles.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from the foreign shareholder or parent entity should be routed through established correspondent banking channels using SWIFT MT103, or SEPA Credit Transfer where the investor is within the Single Euro Payments Area. The remittance information field must contain an explicit equity-capital narrative such as capital contribution to share capital and share premium, or shareholding loan. The French receiving bank will require a completed KYC file, the signed capital-deposit certificate for the SARL's incorporation if the funds are lodged in the statutory blocked account, and a board/shareholder resolution authorising the transaction. For statistical balance-of-payments purposes, the SARL is required to report direct-investment transactions to the Banque de France when the applicable reporting threshold is exceeded (typically EUR 15 million of annual gross foreign-direct-investment flows or the acquisition of a controlling direct-investment relationship); a restaurant-operation injection will almost always remain below this threshold, but the bank must be consulted because threshold definitions are adjusted and the reporting obligation is measured at group level. Verification protocols should include source-of-funds statement, high-resolution scanned invoices or valuation for the paid-in capital, and confirmation that none of the shareholder jurisdictions trigger enhanced sanctions screening.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The principal clearing rails for outbound trade settlements are SEPA Credit Transfer for euro-denominated supplier payments within the EEA, SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfer for non-EUR cross-border payments to suppliers of hotpot ingredients, and irrevocable documentary or commercial letters of credit issued by the SARL's French bank for high-value or first-time vendor relationships in Asia or non-EEA condiment markets. A commercial letter of credit should be issued subject to UCP600, naming the seller as beneficiary and requiring presentation of clean transport documents, commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, and any sanitary or phytosanitary certificate. For smaller recurring payments, an ordinary MT103 must contain the beneficiary bank SWIFT/BIC, IBAN or account number, the bank's correspondent routing references, invoice number, and a purpose narrative matching the underlying food-import contract. Euro interbank settlement is effected through TARGET2 and French SEPA clearing operated by STET for French bulk payments; foreign-currency settlement passes through the French bank's correspondent network and, where applicable, CLS-eligible currency settlement. Funds should never be released without rendering invoices and customs evidence, because French clearing rules and AML controls treat a payment as an independent transaction subject to full traceability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla outright FX forward contracts (EUR/USD, EUR/CNH, EUR/GBP) permitted without exchange-control approval when a deliverable foreign-currency payment for hotpot ingredients or overseas franchise obligations is anticipated and can be documented.

FX swaps and swap-style rollovers executed with a licensed French credit institution to manage temporary mismatches between EUR receipts and USD or CNY payables, subject to the SARL's treasury mandate and an underlying trade exposure.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with onshore capital-account restrictions (for example certain Asian currencies with limited offshore delivery), permitted when executed through an ACPR/ESMA-authorised bank or investment firm and correlated strictly to the SARL's monetary liabilities; speculative NDF positions without physical underlying trade exposure are not acceptable to French compliance departments.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) to hedge medium-term capital or equipment-finance exposure where a non-EUR loan is used to finance restaurant expansion and fit-out, subject to EMIR collateral-margining requirements and board treasury authorisation.

European-style FX options and plain-vanilla collar structures permitted for qualified corporate treasuries, but only when the SARL holds a derivatives trading line, appoints a designated treasury manager, and provides board minutes approving the hedging velocity; options linked to unperformed forecast cash flows are de facto restricted by the bank's suitability and product-governance review under MIFID II.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual financial statements and shareholders' meeting minutes (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the INPI Guichet Unique; registration on the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve the accounts within six months after fiscal year-end; the approved accounts must be filed with the registry within one month after approval. For a 31 December year-end: AGO by 30 June and filing by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to EUR 3,000 against executives for failure to approve accounts; court-ordered injunction with periodic penalty (astreinte); risk of registry administrative strike-off and of criminal liability for repeated non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale, Cerfa 2065 with annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP (Direction Générale des Finances Publiques) through mandatory e-filing channels
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December fiscal year-end: second working day after 1 May of the following year; for any other closing date: within three months of fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of the income tax due (40% if filed after formal notice, 80% in the case of intentional concealment) plus late-payment interest of 0.20% per month

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual and periodic social declarations through the DSN (Déclaration Sociale Nominative)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: URSSAF / MSA via the net-entreprises.fr DSN platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly DSN by the 5th day of the following month; final closing DSN for the calendar year submitted in January of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: URSSAF flat-rate penalty for late or omitted DSN filings plus late-payment increases; failure to report employees may constitute undeclared work and trigger criminal fines and imprisonment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Update of the UBO declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) following any shareholding change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the INPI Guichet Unique; RCS records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any direct or indirect change in beneficial ownership, including share transfers; France does not require a periodic annual UBO re-filing unless a reportable change occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to EUR 7,500 and/or up to six months' imprisonment for knowingly omitting or misstating beneficial-owner information; registry may refuse RCS updates until the UBO file is corrected

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when, at fiscal year-end, the SARL exceeds at least two of three thresholds: total balance sheet EUR 4,000,000; net turnover (exclusive of tax) EUR 8,000,000; average of 50 permanent employees
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général, ANC Regulation n°2016-03) for statutory annual accounts; consolidated accounts under IFRS as adopted in the EU when consolidation is required

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require an annual UBO re-declaration; any share transfer or other change in direct or indirect beneficial ownership must be filed with the RCS Guichet Unique within 30 days. The SARL must keep an up-to-date internal file of beneficial owners and reflect the UBO information in the corporate records; the annual accounts deposit acts as the registry confirmation of the company's continuity.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des mouvements de titres / Share transfer register
Registre des procès-verbaux / Minutes book of shareholders' decisions
Registre des décisions de l'associé unique (applicable to single-member SARL)
Fichier des bénéficiaires effectifs / Beneficial-owner file

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 – 1,100 per year (commercial domiciliation service fee in France)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – 15,000 per year for a typical full statutory audit engagement of a restaurant SARL

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit (up to 30% of eligible expenses), SME reduced rate (15% on first €42,500 taxable profit), investment tax credits

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Déclaration de résultat IS (Form 1200) via impots.gouv.fr electronic filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: By the 15th day of the 4th month following fiscal year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report French-source income only if applicable
Include all sales and services rendered in France

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 0.75% per month of tax due up to 10% maximum plus possible criminal sanctions

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 12.8% (reduced to 0% under many double tax treaties for EU/EEA residents with TRC)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and submit relevant forms via impots.gouv.fr
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0%-10% per treaty; Interest: 0%-10% per treaty, often 0% for related parties

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €50 million annual turnover or €43 million total assets triggers local file and master file
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: French Economic Substance Law requires adequate economic substance for certain entities with penalties for non-compliance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain contemporaneous TP documentation or apply non-arm's length pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €75,000 per infringement plus 5% of adjustment amount and interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for restitution, disqualification, and criminal liability under tax evasion provisions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting or misstating revenue in the tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties of 80% of evaded tax plus interest, possible imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, fines, and obligation to pay tax plus penalties

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Not withholding dividend or royalty WHT on payments to non-resident entities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty equal to WHT due plus 10% surcharge plus possible criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable to pay withheld tax and penalties, possible jail time

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a company without real business activities or decision-making in France
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €75,000, potential dissolution, and tax reassessment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for damages, possible criminal sanctions including imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a shell company to avoid tax by lacking commercial reality or substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion sanctions including fines and imprisonment plus civil penalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil leading to personal restitution, travel bans, and up to 5 years imprisonment
